r: yǒu qí fù bì yǒu qí zǐ
mean: like father, like son: children take after their parents
lit: where there is such a father, there is bound to be such a son

use.how: Said as a comment on a child who shows a parent's talent, habit or fault: 真是有其父必有其子。 It can be praise or a dig, depending on the trait.

near.diff: 上梁不正下梁歪 blames juniors' bad behaviour on a bad example from above; 有其父必有其子 just notes that a child resembles a parent, for good or ill.

cue: At a party, a famous chef's twelve-year-old son cooks a dish every bit as good as his dad's. What do the guests remark?

ctx.s: 儿子跟他爸一样爱踢足球，真是{有其父必有其子}。
ctx.en: His son loves football just as much as he does. Like father, like son.

ctx.s: 他爸爸是有名的医生，他也考上了医学院，{有其父必有其子}啊。
ctx.en: His father is a well-known doctor, and he got into medical school too. Like father, like son.

ctx.s: “这孩子说话的样子跟他爸一模一样！”“{有其父必有其子}嘛。”
ctx.en: "The way this kid talks is exactly like his dad!" "Well, like father, like son."

ctx.s: 老张年轻时脾气就急，现在儿子也这样，邻居都说{有其父必有其子}。
ctx.en: Old Zhang had a quick temper when he was young, and now his son is the same; the neighbours all say the apple doesn't fall far from the tree.

ctx.s: 小王跟他父亲一样，一聊起钓鱼就停不下来，同事们笑着说：“{有其父必有其子}。”
ctx.en: Just like his father, Xiao Wang can't stop once he starts talking about fishing; his colleagues laugh and say: "Like father, like son."

ctx.s: 报道写道，这位年轻棋手的父亲也曾是全国冠军，可谓{有其父必有其子}。
ctx.en: The report noted that the young chess player's father had also been a national champion: truly like father, like son.

bad.s: 我和我哥长得很像，{有其父必有其子}。
bad.en: (meant: my brother and I look very alike)
bad.why: It is about a child taking after a parent, not about brothers or sisters resembling each other.

bad.s: 他爸爸很高，他却很矮，真是{有其父必有其子}。
bad.en: (meant: his father is tall, but he is short)
bad.why: The saying states a resemblance, so it cannot describe a son who is the opposite of his father.

r: shǒu xīn shǒu bèi dōu shì ròu
mean: they are all equally dear to me; I can't favour one over another
lit: the palm and the back of the hand are both my own flesh

use.how: Said, usually by a parent, when pressed to choose between or favour one of several people equally close to them: 手心手背都是肉，我哪个都舍不得。

cue: A mother of two sons is asked which one she loves more, and she refuses to choose between them. What does she say?

ctx.s: 两个孩子我都爱，{手心手背都是肉}。
ctx.en: I love both my children; they're equally dear to me.

ctx.s: 你问我更疼哪个孙子？{手心手背都是肉}，哪能分得出来！
ctx.en: You're asking which grandson I dote on more? They're both my flesh and blood; how could I pick?

ctx.s: 姐妹俩吵架，妈妈谁也不想偏向，只能叹气：“{手心手背都是肉}啊。”
ctx.en: The two sisters were quarrelling and their mother didn't want to take sides; she could only sigh: "You're both my children."

ctx.s: 爸爸要把房子留给哪个儿子，一直下不了决心，毕竟{手心手背都是肉}。
ctx.en: Dad could never decide which son to leave the house to; after all, he loved them both the same.

ctx.s: 两个都是我带出来的徒弟，{手心手背都是肉}，让我只选一个，太难了。
ctx.en: I trained both of these apprentices myself; they're equally dear to me, and asking me to pick just one is too hard.

ctx.s: 老师说，班里的学生对她来说{手心手背都是肉}，不会偏向成绩好的。
ctx.en: The teacher said every student in her class is equally dear to her, and she won't favour the ones with good grades.

bad.s: 这两家餐厅{手心手背都是肉}，你随便选吧。
bad.en: (meant: both restaurants are equally good, pick either)
bad.why: It is about people you love equally, usually your own children, not about two equally good options.

bad.s: 他把钱都给了大儿子，真是{手心手背都是肉}。
bad.en: (meant: he gave all the money to his eldest son)
bad.why: The saying claims equal love and is used to refuse favouritism, so it cannot describe favouring one child.

r: jiā chǒu bù kě wài yáng
mean: a family's shameful affairs should not be told to outsiders
lit: a family's ugly matters must not be spread outside

use.how: Given as a reason to keep a family's, or by extension a group's, embarrassing problems from outsiders: 这事家丑不可外扬。 Also quoted critically when it is used to hide wrongdoing.

cue: Your uncle has run up big gambling debts, and your mother warns you not to breathe a word of it to the neighbours. What principle does she invoke?

ctx.s: 爸妈吵架的事别跟同学说，{家丑不可外扬}。
ctx.en: Don't tell your classmates that Mum and Dad were fighting. What happens in the family stays in the family.

ctx.s: 奶奶总说{家丑不可外扬}，家里有矛盾从来不让外人知道。
ctx.en: Grandma always says family shame stays at home; she never lets outsiders know about any trouble in the family.

ctx.s: “你哥欠钱的事要不要告诉邻居？”“算了吧，{家丑不可外扬}。”
ctx.en: "Should we tell the neighbours about your brother's debts?" "Better not. You don't air the family's dirty laundry."

ctx.s: 公司内部出了问题，老板却想着{家丑不可外扬}，要求员工不准对外透露。
ctx.en: There was trouble inside the company, but the boss wanted to keep it in-house and told staff not to say a word outside.

ctx.s: 她犹豫了很久才开口，毕竟{家丑不可外扬}，可这次她实在忍不下去了。
ctx.en: She hesitated a long time before speaking up; you don't air family troubles, after all, but this time she just couldn't bear it any more.

ctx.s: 专家提醒，家庭暴力不是私事，不能拿{家丑不可外扬}当借口。
ctx.en: Experts warn that domestic violence is not a private matter, and keeping family shame hidden is no excuse.

bad.s: 我考了第一名，{家丑不可外扬}，先别告诉别人。
bad.en: (meant: I came first in the exam, but don't tell anyone yet)
bad.why: The saying is about something shameful in the family; good news is not shameful, so there is nothing to hide.

bad.s: 他把公司的核心技术卖给了对手，真是{家丑不可外扬}。
bad.en: (meant: he sold the company's key technology to a rival)
bad.why: The saying tells people to keep embarrassing matters inside; it does not describe leaking secrets, which are not shameful affairs.

r: huò bǐ sān jiā bù chī kuī
mean: compare several sellers before you buy
lit: compare the goods at three shops and you won't lose out

use.how: Said as advice before a purchase, or to explain why one is shopping around: 别急着买，货比三家不吃亏。 三 just means several.

near.diff: 一分钱一分货 says that a higher price buys better quality; 货比三家不吃亏 says to compare several sellers before deciding.

cue: Your friend is about to buy the first laptop she sees in the first shop. You suggest checking a few other stores first. What saying backs you up?

ctx.s: 先别买，再去别的店看看，{货比三家不吃亏}。
ctx.en: Don't buy it yet; let's look in other shops. It pays to shop around.

ctx.s: 买手机我一般会在网上多看几家，{货比三家不吃亏}嘛。
ctx.en: When I buy a phone I usually check a few sellers online. Comparing never hurts.

ctx.s: “这家的价格已经不错了吧？”“{货比三家不吃亏}，明天再问问别家。”
ctx.en: "This shop's price is pretty good already, isn't it?" "It pays to compare. Let's ask a few others tomorrow."

ctx.s: 装修房子前，他跑了五家建材市场，说{货比三家不吃亏}。
ctx.en: Before renovating his flat he went round five building-supply markets, saying you never lose by shopping around.

ctx.s: 公司采购办公用品也讲究{货比三家不吃亏}，至少要拿到三份报价。
ctx.en: Even when the company buys office supplies it follows the rule of shopping around: at least three quotes are required.

ctx.s: 妈妈买菜从来不在第一个摊位停下，她的口头禅就是{货比三家不吃亏}。
ctx.en: Mum never stops at the first stall when she buys vegetables; her motto is that it pays to compare.

bad.s: 他只吃这家店的面，{货比三家不吃亏}。
bad.en: (meant: he only eats the noodles at this one shop)
bad.why: The saying urges comparing several sellers, so it cannot back up sticking loyally to one.

bad.s: 我们班这三个同学，{货比三家不吃亏}，看看谁成绩最好。
bad.en: (meant: let's compare these three classmates and see whose grades are best)
bad.why: It is about shopping: comparing goods and prices before buying, not comparing people.

r: yǒu qián néng shǐ guǐ tuī mò
mean: with enough money you can get anyone to do anything
lit: if you have money, you can even make a ghost turn the millstone

use.how: Said cynically or wryly about money getting done what otherwise would not be done, often after 真是 or 以为: 真是有钱能使鬼推磨。

cue: A restaurant that told everyone it was fully booked suddenly finds a table when a rich man slips the manager a thick envelope. What do the people waiting mutter?

ctx.s: 一加钱，师傅马上就来修了，真是{有钱能使鬼推磨}。
ctx.en: As soon as we offered more money, the repairman came right over. Money really does talk.

ctx.s: 刚才还说没房间，给了小费就有了，{有钱能使鬼推磨}啊！
ctx.en: A minute ago they had no rooms, and after a tip there's one. Money can buy anything!

ctx.s: 他总以为{有钱能使鬼推磨}，结果这次花再多钱也没用。
ctx.en: He always thought money could make anyone do anything, but this time no amount of money helped.

ctx.s: “他的手续怎么这么快就办好了？”“你说呢？{有钱能使鬼推磨}呗。”
ctx.en: "How did his paperwork get done so fast?" "What do you think? Money gets things moving."

ctx.s: 小说里的老板相信{有钱能使鬼推磨}，可到最后连家人都离开了他。
ctx.en: The boss in the novel believes money can buy anything, yet in the end even his family leaves him.

ctx.s: 有人说{有钱能使鬼推磨}，但真正的朋友是用钱买不来的。
ctx.en: Some say money can make anyone do anything, but true friends can't be bought.

bad.s: 他努力赚钱养家，真是{有钱能使鬼推磨}。
bad.en: (meant: he works hard to earn money for his family)
bad.why: The saying is a cynical remark about money making others do one's bidding; it is not praise for earning a living.

bad.s: 这个月工资涨了，{有钱能使鬼推磨}，我好开心。
bad.en: (meant: I got a pay rise this month and I'm so happy)
bad.why: It is not about the joy of having money but about money buying other people's help or cooperation.

t: 人往高处走，水往低处流
r: rén wǎng gāo chù zǒu, shuǐ wǎng dī chù liú
mean: it's only natural for people to seek a better position
lit: people walk toward higher places, water flows toward lower ones

use.how: Said to explain or accept someone leaving for a better job, school or city, usually with understanding rather than blame: 人往高处走，水往低处流，他跳槽很正常。

cue: Your best employee tells you she has an offer from a bigger firm at double the pay. You don't hold it against her. What do you say?

ctx.s: 他去了更好的公司，{人往高处走，水往低处流}嘛。
ctx.en: He moved to a better company. Everyone wants to get ahead, after all.

ctx.s: 女儿想去大城市发展，妈妈虽然不舍，也知道{人往高处走，水往低处流}。
ctx.en: The daughter wants to build her career in a big city; her mother hates to let her go, but knows it's natural to aim higher.

ctx.s: “小李要辞职了，你不生气吗？”“{人往高处走，水往低处流}，我祝福他。”
ctx.en: "Xiao Li is quitting. Aren't you angry?" "People naturally go where things are better. I wish him well."

ctx.s: 村里的年轻人都去城里打工了，老人们说，{人往高处走，水往低处流}，留不住的。
ctx.en: The young people have all gone to work in the cities; the old folk say it's only natural to seek a better life, and you can't keep them.

ctx.s: {人往高处走，水往低处流}，想换个更好的平台，这没什么丢人的。
ctx.en: It's natural to want to move up; wanting a better platform is nothing to be ashamed of.

ctx.s: 老板明白{人往高处走，水往低处流}，所以用加薪和培训来留住人才。
ctx.en: The boss understands that people will always look for something better, so he keeps talent with raises and training.

bad.s: 他被公司降职了，真是{人往高处走，水往低处流}。
bad.en: (meant: he was demoted)
bad.why: It explains people moving up to something better, not someone dropping to a lower position.

bad.s: 我们周末去爬山吧，{人往高处走，水往低处流}。
bad.en: (meant: let's go hiking at the weekend)
bad.why: The higher place is a better job or life, not a literal mountain.

r: xīn guān shàng rèn sān bǎ huǒ
mean: a new boss always starts with a burst of vigorous changes
lit: a new official, on taking office, lights three fires

use.how: Said, often wryly, about a newly appointed leader making a flurry of changes or tough rules at the start: 新官上任三把火，你看他这几天忙的。

near.diff: 一朝天子一朝臣 says a new leader brings in their own people; 新官上任三把火 says a new leader opens with a burst of reforms and strictness.

cue: Your department gets a new director, and in her first week she bans phones in meetings, changes the schedule and starts spot checks. How do colleagues sum it up?

ctx.s: 新校长一来就改了作息时间，{新官上任三把火}嘛。
ctx.en: The new principal changed the timetable the moment she arrived. A new broom sweeps clean.

ctx.s: “新主任要求每天八点开会。”“{新官上任三把火}，过一阵就好了。”
ctx.en: "The new director wants a meeting at eight every day." "New bosses always start out fired up. It'll settle down."

ctx.s: 他刚当上队长就定了一堆新规矩，大家笑他{新官上任三把火}。
ctx.en: He'd barely become captain before he laid down a pile of new rules, and everyone teased him about the new-boss zeal.

ctx.s: 都说{新官上任三把火}，可新经理来了一个月，什么都没改。
ctx.en: They say a new boss always shakes things up, but the new manager has been here a month and hasn't changed a thing.

ctx.s: 新市长一上任就连推三项改革，真应了那句{新官上任三把火}。
ctx.en: The new mayor launched three reforms in a row right after taking office, just as the saying about new officials goes.

ctx.s: 我刚当上组长，不想搞{新官上任三把火}那一套，打算先听听大家的意见。
ctx.en: I've just become team leader, and I don't want to do the new-boss shake-up thing; I plan to hear everyone out first.

bad.s: 他刚来公司当实习生，{新官上任三把火}，特别努力。
bad.en: (meant: he's a new intern and works really hard)
bad.why: It is about a new boss or official imposing changes, not a low-ranking newcomer working hard.

bad.s: 新经理今天发了很大的脾气，{新官上任三把火}。
bad.en: (meant: the new manager lost his temper badly today)
bad.why: The fires are reforms and tough measures at the start of a term, not a fit of anger.

r: sān gè hé shang méi shuǐ chī
mean: when a job belongs to everyone, nobody ends up doing it
lit: three monks, and no water to drink

story.text: The saying is the last line of a three-step folk rhyme: one monk carries his own water, two monks carry it together, three monks have no water to drink. Alone, a monk fetches water himself with two buckets on a shoulder pole; two monks carry one bucket slung between them; with three, each waits for the others to go, and nobody fetches any. The rhyme became widely known through the 1980 Shanghai Animation Film Studio cartoon Three Monks.
story.source: folk rhyme 一个和尚挑水吃，两个和尚抬水吃，三个和尚没水吃; animated film 《三个和尚》 (1980)

use.how: Said about a group in which shared responsibility means nobody acts; sometimes the fuller rhyme is quoted. 人多了，反而三个和尚没水吃。

near.diff: 众人拾柴火焰高 praises many people all contributing; 三个和尚没水吃 criticises many people each leaving the job to someone else.

cue: Four flatmates share a kitchen; each assumes someone else will take out the rubbish, and it piles up for two weeks. What sums it up?

ctx.s: 宿舍的垃圾一个星期没人倒，真是{三个和尚没水吃}。
ctx.en: Nobody in the dorm has taken out the rubbish for a week. Everybody's job is nobody's job.

ctx.s: 这件事最好指定一个负责人，不然{三个和尚没水吃}。
ctx.en: We'd better put one person in charge of this, or with everyone responsible, nothing will get done.

ctx.s: “办公室的饮水机谁去换水？”“谁都不去，{三个和尚没水吃}呗。”
ctx.en: "Who's going to change the office water cooler?" "Nobody. Everyone leaves it to everyone else."

ctx.s: 项目组加了人，进度反而更慢了，大家互相推，成了{三个和尚没水吃}。
ctx.en: The project team got more people, but progress actually slowed; everyone passed the buck and nothing got done.

ctx.s: 小区的路灯坏了半年，物业和居委会都说不归自己管，{三个和尚没水吃}。
ctx.en: The streetlight in our estate has been broken for six months; the management company and the residents' committee both say it's not their job, so nobody fixes it.

ctx.s: 管理学课上，老师用{三个和尚没水吃}的例子说明责任必须分清。
ctx.en: In management class, the teacher used the three-monks story to show that responsibilities must be clearly assigned.

bad.s: 我们三个人一起努力，{三个和尚没水吃}，很快就完成了。
bad.en: (meant: the three of us worked together and finished quickly)
bad.why: It describes a group where nobody does the job, the opposite of successful teamwork.

bad.s: 家里停水了，{三个和尚没水吃}。
bad.en: (meant: the water supply at home has been cut off)
bad.why: It is not about actually lacking water but about people shirking a shared duty.

r: zhòng rén shí chái huǒ yàn gāo
mean: when everyone pitches in, together they achieve far more
lit: when everyone gathers firewood, the flames burn high

use.how: Said to call for or praise joint effort, often in team pep talks, appeals and donation drives: 大家一起出力，众人拾柴火焰高。

near.t: 三个臭皮匠，顶个诸葛亮
near.diff: 三个臭皮匠，顶个诸葛亮 is about pooling ideas to solve a problem; 众人拾柴火焰高 is about everyone contributing effort or resources.
三个和尚没水吃 is the failure case, where a crowd shirks the job; 众人拾柴火焰高 is the success case, where everyone contributes.

cue: A classmate's family can't afford an operation, so everyone at school gives a little, and together it covers the whole cost. What saying fits?

ctx.s: 大家都出一点力，{众人拾柴火焰高}嘛。
ctx.en: Let's all do our bit. Many hands make light work.

ctx.s: 一个人搬不完，叫上邻居一起，{众人拾柴火焰高}，半天就搬好了。
ctx.en: One person couldn't have moved it all, but with the neighbours pitching in, it was done in half a day.

ctx.s: “这么多活儿，我们几个干得完吗？”“放心，{众人拾柴火焰高}。”
ctx.en: "Can just a few of us get all this work done?" "Don't worry. If we all pitch in, we will."

ctx.s: 全村每家捐一点，{众人拾柴火焰高}，终于修好了那座桥。
ctx.en: Every household in the village gave a little, and together they finally got the bridge repaired.

ctx.s: 倡议书最后写道：{众人拾柴火焰高}，期待每一位居民的参与。
ctx.en: The appeal ended: when everyone contributes, we achieve far more; we hope every resident will take part.

ctx.s: 球队没有明星球员，靠的是团结，正所谓{众人拾柴火焰高}。
ctx.en: The team had no star players; it relied on unity. As they say, when everyone adds fuel, the fire burns high.

bad.s: 他一个人熬夜完成了全部工作，真是{众人拾柴火焰高}。
bad.en: (meant: he stayed up all night and finished all the work by himself)
bad.why: It credits many people contributing together, not one person working alone.

bad.s: 地铁里人太多了，挤得要命，{众人拾柴火焰高}。
bad.en: (meant: the subway is packed and terribly crowded)
bad.why: It praises joint effort toward a goal, not a mere crowd of people.

t: 台上一分钟，台下十年功
r: tái shàng yī fēn zhōng, tái xià shí nián gōng
mean: a brief moment of brilliance rests on years of practice
lit: one minute on the stage, ten years of training off it

use.how: Said in admiration of a performance, match or skill that looks effortless, pointing to the long practice behind it: 他弹得这么好，真是台上一分钟，台下十年功。

near.t: 只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针
near.diff: 铁杵磨成针 encourages someone to persevere at a hard task; 台上一分钟，台下十年功 explains a polished performance by the years of practice behind it.

cue: After a gymnast's flawless ninety-second routine, the commentator reminds viewers that she has trained daily since she was five. What saying does he use?

ctx.s: 她跳得这么好，{台上一分钟，台下十年功}啊。
ctx.en: She dances so beautifully. Behind every minute on stage are years of practice.

ctx.s: 别看魔术师变得那么轻松，{台上一分钟，台下十年功}。
ctx.en: The magician makes it look so easy, but that ease takes years of practice.

ctx.s: “他演讲怎么一点都不紧张？”“{台上一分钟，台下十年功}，他私下练了很多遍。”
ctx.en: "How come he's not nervous at all when he speaks?" "It looks easy because he's practised it over and over in private."

ctx.s: 京剧老师常对学生说：“{台上一分钟，台下十年功}，基本功一天也不能停。”
ctx.en: The Peking opera teacher often tells students: "Every minute on stage rests on ten years of work behind the scenes; never skip a day of basic training."

ctx.s: 冠军那套动作只有两分钟，正所谓{台上一分钟，台下十年功}，她从五岁就开始练了。
ctx.en: The champion's routine lasted only two minutes, but as they say, a moment of brilliance takes years of work: she started training at five.

ctx.s: 很多人只看到明星的风光，却不明白{台上一分钟，台下十年功}的道理。
ctx.en: Many people only see a star's glamour and don't understand that it rests on years of hard work.

bad.s: 这次考试我没复习，{台上一分钟，台下十年功}，结果考砸了。
bad.en: (meant: I didn't revise for the exam and failed)
bad.why: It praises the long practice behind a fine performance; it cannot describe a failure caused by no preparation.

bad.s: 电影太长了，{台上一分钟，台下十年功}。
bad.en: (meant: the film felt endlessly long)
bad.why: The numbers contrast a short performance with long training; they say nothing about time dragging.
